claim: Two views each with exactly zero cross-covariance with the same signal have exactly zero cross-covariance under concatenation
label: algebraic
assumptions: same joint law/rows, same weights and same centring for every score; exact zero (not approximate)
notes: Holds for population or empirical law alike; implies neither independence nor any nonlinear guarantee

claim: Affine maps of a view preserve zero cross-covariance with the signal
label: algebraic
assumptions: map affine and fixed (not fitted on the evaluation rows)
notes: Cov(Ah+b, S)=A Cov(h,S)

claim: Nonlinear processing can break exact-zero composition (SV and V each zero covariance with S, product recovers S)
label: algebraic
assumptions: independent symmetric signs V,S
notes: Exact counterexample

claim: Zero affine least-squares R2 forces every linear threshold classifier to majority accuracy (retired claim)
label: unsupported
notes: Refuted by a 20-row counterexample (R2=0, 18/20 threshold accuracy); API retired on fix branch only (origin/main still ships it per CLAIM_LEDGER O2)

claim: Zero cross-covariance means no affine predictor improves on the best constant under any loss convex in the affine prediction
label: population under assumptions
assumptions: finite first moments; categorical or one-hot target; loss convex in the affine score (LEACE Thm); applies to the empirical law if computed in-sample
notes: Thresholded accuracy is not such a loss

claim: Approximate composition: R2(h_1..h_k) <= sum_p R2(h_p)/lambda_min(R), tight
label: algebraic
assumptions: nonsingular per-view covariances; same rows and centring; ridge version needs the same tau in every score (guarantee-review AMENDMENT_2026-09-23_ridge_premise.md)
notes: Rayleigh-Ritz; tight on the delta example; ridge-premise caution in claims-foundation T3-12 was too strong and is superseded

claim: Pooled one-hot R2 equals the prevalence-weighted average of per-class OvR R2
label: algebraic
assumptions: both scores share rows, centring and ridge penalty
notes: Not original (variance-weighted multi-output R2); dominant axis is only a lower bound on the best linear sensitive direction

claim: Under Z-T-(S,C) and a fixed fitted law, each conditional MI is convex in Q so the feasible set is convex and the objective linear
label: algebraic
assumptions: fixed joint law p(s,c,t); Z depends on data only through T
notes: Standard (Calmon-Fawaz 2012); no new optimisation result

claim: Zero-budget conditional constraint is linear in Q
label: algebraic
assumptions: fixed fitted law; I(S;Z|C)=0 iff sum_t [p(s,c,t)-p(s|c)p(c,t)] Q_tz = 0
notes: privacy_matrix docstring states the iff

claim: I(S;Z|C)=I(S;Z,C)-I(S;C), so conditional budgets are joint-view budgets with a shifted constant
label: algebraic
assumptions: C is the conditioning variable actually used — the 2-cell (A) or 4-cell (AB) coarse partition of the fitted model, not the released continuous H
notes: Scope caveat: "joint-view" means (Z, coarse C), not the recipient view (Z, H)

claim: The selected release satisfies I_Q(S;Z|C_A) <= 0.01 on the fitted finite model
label: finite-sample under assumptions
assumptions: plug-in fitted law on mechanism rows; 2-cell k-means partition of H_A columns [1,3]; numerical tolerance
notes: Held-out coarse plug-in CMI on 2018 attacker-validation people is 0.0127-0.0247 and four-cell 0.0164-0.0209 (objective-diagnosis OBJECTIVE_DIAGNOSIS.md:38-39) — the budget does not transfer even at the coarse level; continuous-H CMI unidentified

claim: Optimality of the fitted programme is solver-reported, not certified (no duality gap recorded)
label: finite-sample under assumptions
assumptions: fitted programme; floating point
notes: Superseded after the manuscript commit: objective-diagnosis SOLVER_CERTIFICATE puts Q within 1.27e-7 nats of the fitted optimum via a nonnegative-multiplier lower bound (floating-point, not interval arithmetic)

claim: Information-radius / capacity bound: I(S;Z|W) <= kappa (radius = capacity of the fixed public kernel) for every joint law and every view W determining the kernel public state
label: population under assumptions
assumptions: fixed code and kernel; release randomness independent of all data (one persistent draw); kernel may depend on b(H_A) but not H_B; support conditions
notes: The only distribution-free bound in the lineage; established mathematics (Gallager-Ryabko, Csiszar). D17 kappa is vacuous (log 17)

claim: I(S;Z|H) <= I(T;Z|H) <= sum_t p_t KL(Q_t || sum_u p_u Q_u) described as "distribution-free"
label: population under assumptions
assumptions: Markov H-T-Z (Z depends only on T); p_t must be the population marginal of T — with 2018 mechanism state masses it is a plug-in
notes: "Distribution-free" is wrong for the p_t-weighted form; only the radius/capacity (max over p_t) is distribution-free (guarantee review)

claim: Attribute-specific bound I(S;Z|W) <= eta_TV log|S|
label: population under assumptions
assumptions: as the radius bound; full-H attribute certificates additionally need T independent of H given (S,B) or H-smoothness, which T0 violates by construction
notes: Not a PCRL theorem

claim: Absolute recovery (entropy baseline minus held-out loss of an attacker fixed before evaluation) lower-bounds the view MI up to sampling error
label: finite-sample under assumptions
assumptions: attacker frozen before evaluation; held-out rows; baseline equals the true marginal entropy; iid rows
notes: Never tabulated in the manuscript for Q, despite :187 "We report absolute recovery beside every increment"

claim: The increment over the H-restricted fit bounds I(S;Z|H) in neither direction
label: algebraic
notes: Correct; counterexample Z=f(H)

claim: Binning a conditioning view can drop a full log 2 of measured leakage to zero
label: algebraic
assumptions: exact fixture
notes: Fixture retained in test suite (replacement AMENDMENT_1 M2)

claim: Appending T to J=(Y,S) adds exactly zero task information while replacing J by T keeps the task and removes log 2 of sensitive disclosure
label: algebraic
assumptions: H constant; discrete exact joint
notes: Design example, not an ACS finding

claim: A deterministic append [H_A,Z_J,R] can only weakly increase Bayes-optimal sensitive recovery over [H_A,Z_J]
label: population under assumptions
assumptions: Bayes-optimal (not finite) attackers; same population law
notes: Every measured decrease under an append is a finite-attacker artefact

claim: Preservation of the published service is an identity; service bytes identical across all 30 family/anchor interfaces
label: empirical under listed recipients
assumptions: concatenation design; byte check on the 30 evaluated interfaces
notes: Bytes, not accuracy (2016 accuracies 0.874/0.891/0.760 recounted)

label: empirical under listed recipients
assumptions: 2018 development pools reused; conditional on fitted releases and validation-selected probes; household bootstrap over the 5,473-household union of three anchor test pools

claim: All eight sensitive point estimates favour Q over J; 7/8 adjusted non-inferiority bounds unresolved at the +0.001 cap
label: empirical under listed recipients
assumptions: registered attacker slate; J-relative increments; Bonferroni-706
notes: Recounted. Q recovery over H is positive on 8/8 (0.00086-0.00614) — not reported

claim: 2016: each release passes 8/10 registered clauses; all eight sensitive upper bounds below zero; task upper bounds above -0.003
label: empirical under listed recipients

notes: Recounted. Sensitive clauses cap recovery in excess of J (main.tex:365 wording "added recovery" is the P-1 error). Q recovery beyond H positive 8/8, 6/8 unadjusted intervals exclude zero

claim: All eight sensitive bounds and both task signs also hold under Bonferroni over the 20 primary endpoints

notes: Strongest correct simultaneous reading; not a registered decision

notes: "Matched" = interface-matched, not matched on task loss or disclosure
